text: Lists are ordered collections of items, wrapped in square brackets and separated by commas.
Each item can be any type, [shush] numbers, strings, floats, booleans, even mixed together.
Print a list and you see all its elements at once.
Lists can even hold other lists, letting you build tables and grids nested inside one another.
Len tells you how many items are in the list.
Unlike strings, lists are mutable — append adds a new item straight onto the end.
[sniff] And remove deletes the first matching item it finds.
[cough] You can also count how many times a value appears, or find its position with the index method.
The in keyword checks membership instantly, and plus concatenates two lists into a new one.
Finally, sort rearranges the list in place, [chuckle] reverse equals True flips it largest to smallest.
Video 6 tackles indexing. Comment PYTHON if you want the cheat sheet.
